docs.title: Protocols — Adopting a Protocol Using a Synthesized Implementation

hints: If you customise `==`, you must hash exactly the same data.
Compute a normalised form (lowercase, strip dots and `+suffix` from the local part) and use it in both `==` and `hash(into:)`.
jsBridge: Custom `==` and `hash(into:)` must agree: equal values **must** have equal hashes. JS `Set`/`Map` can't use custom equality at all (identity or primitives only). Swift lets you define identity for your domain, like Gmail-style email rules.

compass.q: JS devs normalise to a string key for Map lookups. When is a custom `Hashable` better than storing a normalised string?
